reading.body:
CyrusOne's Aurora campus publishes 114 MW of IT capacity, the largest disclosed figure in Illinois and 48 percent of the state's 236 MW public total.

The number matters less as a measure of Illinois than as a measure of disclosure. Only six Illinois facilities publish capacity at all, while 44 other mapped data centers publish nothing, so the state's real installed base is unknown and almost certainly larger than 236 MW. A single campus holding nearly half of a published total is a sign of how thin that total is, not of how concentrated the state is.

For AI specifically, 114 MW across 450,000 square feet of technical space can house a meaningful training cluster but not a frontier hyperscale build. The rack count of roughly 2,850 is an estimate derived from an assumed 40 kW per rack, not a disclosed specification, and actual density depends on tenant mix and cooling. What the data does not cover is the part that decides whether this campus scales: power availability and grid interconnection at Aurora, tenant occupancy, and power purchase terms. The site holds Green Globes certification, which speaks to environmental management rather than to the electrical headroom that constrains AI growth.
